# Kenneth Loi

> UC Berkeley Biophysics graduate student in the Doudna Lab, focused on programmable biology, RNA-guided systems, structural discovery, selfish genetic elements, and computational acceleration for biological discovery and design.

## About

Southern California kid raised on science fiction and beef noodle soup.

I'm drawn to the strange moments when biology invents new primitives: genetic parasites becoming CRISPR, endosymbionts becoming organelles, retroviruses becoming placentas. Evolution has a habit of turning weirdness into infrastructure.

I look for that pattern everywhere. Science creates the 0-to-1s; the world scales them into 1-to-1000s. Progress is rate-limited by the former.

I want to spend my life working on both. If you're working on the zeroes, let's chat.

## Research Themes

- Programmable biology: designing and reprogramming molecular systems for detection, regulation, and computation.
- Structural discovery: studying structures conserved across hundreds of millions of years.
- Selfish genes: studying genetic conflict to understand biomolecular innovations.
- Computational acceleration: leveraging computational techniques to discover and design new biology.
